subject: Annualize ladder + burn smoothing — renewal amendment and co-term request
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acmedata.com>, Chris Lee <chris.lee@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annualize ladder + burn smoothing — renewal amendment and co-term request

Hi Sarah / Chris —

Following our QBR, I wanted to propose a structure that should address Acme's predictability needs while giving you runway for ramp: a 3-year annualized ladder with an embedded burn-smoothing mechanism and an optional auto-renew opt-out window. High-level: 
- Year 1: 60% of committed units to accommodate front-loaded PoC / ramping projects.
- Year 2: 30% increase over Year 1 baseline if the growth milestone (30% QoQ usage increase for two consecutive quarters) is met.
- Year 3: step-up to full steady-state commitment.

We'd bill monthly with a quarterly true-up and provide credits for over/under variance to smooth budget impact. Co-terming: I see you mentioned another vendor renewal in Q1 2027 — if you'd like, we can align the amendment to co-term at 2027-03-31 and prorate the first year accordingly.

Attached is a draft workbook with the ramp math (ACME_Renewal_Workbook.xlsx). If this structure looks roughly right, Marissa and I will draft a formal amendment and a short SOW for the expected capacity increases.

Next steps: could you confirm the target co-term date and the preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. annual invoice)? Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0156

Attachment: ACME_Renewal_Workbook.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

From: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acmedata.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Lee <chris.lee@acmedata.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annualize ladder + burn smoothing — renewal amendment and co-term request

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from Acme procurement: 
1) Our current external vendor co-term ends 2027-03-31, so co-terming to that date is ideal.
2) We expect a heavy Q1 2027 usage spike for a pilot we're running, so frontloading in Year 1 makes sense, but finance wants a clear smoothing mechanism so budget owners don't see unpredictable spikes.
3) Billing cadence: finance prefers monthly invoices with a consolidated annual true-up.

Can you confirm how credits would be applied at true-up (cash credit vs. invoice offset) and what the proposed penalty/true-up window is if usage materially exceeds committed capacity?

Also, we will need an SOW for capacity + a short security pack (SOC2 cert, retention details) before procurement will sign. Looping Chris for his input on co-term logistics.

—Sarah
Sarah Gomez
Head of Procurement, Acme DataOps
sarah.gomez@acmedata.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annualize ladder + burn smoothing — renewal amendment and co-term request

Hi Sarah — great flags. A few operational points from our side: 
- Credits: we apply invoice offsets at quarterly true-up by default; cash credits can be arranged for enterprise contracts on request (we'll note this in the amendment).
- Penalty/true-up window: proposed model is a 90-day rolling true-up with a 20% grace buffer; anything above that is invoiced at the overage rate (list rate).
- Co-term mechanics: we can prorate Year 1 to 2027-03-31 and then present Year 2/3 as full-year commitments aligned to the new anniversary.

I'm attaching a draft amendment that reflects the above so you can get internal review: proposed_amendment_draft.pdf. This includes an optional section that converts auto-renew into an opt-out clause at 60 days prior to renewal so your legal team can evaluate the change.

If that sounds ok, let's schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the finance/legal teams through the workbook and amendment.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed_amendment_draft.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annualize ladder + burn smoothing — renewal amendment and co-term request

Thanks Sarah — and thanks Marissa for the draft. 

Short answers: invoice offsets at quarterly true-up (standard), 90-day rolling true-up with 20% buffer for overage billing, and we will provide a security supplement (SOC2 Type II report + retention table) as a separate pack.

A few refinements to propose for the amendment to make it practical for both teams: 
- Billing: monthly invoices, consolidated annual true-up, with overage invoiced quarterly.
- Smoothing: at each quarterly true-up we will calculate variance and apply a smoothing credit equal to 50% of the negative variance (i.e., if you used 20% less than committed, 10% credit applied immediately; the remainder carried forward for annual true-up). This reduces budget shock while allowing us to reconcile usage fairly.
- Performance incentive: if Acme exceeds the Year 2 growth milestone (30% QoQ for two consecutive quarters), we will apply a 5% credit on Year 3 committed cost.

If that framework is acceptable, I'll put a redline in the amendment and Marissa will start the DocuSign flow. Proposed next step: 30-min call Wed 08:30 PT. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Stephanie
